observations.statement: The ray-fiber argument normalizes the base residue to remove further unit ambiguity, identifies norm-one commutators and the cyclotomic quotient, and proves disjointness by inertia. At most four elements are lost in each norm fiber. The logarithmic lower bound dominates the obstruction tail after choosing one fixed cutoff, before the field-dependent asymptotic limit and subsequent thin-width diagonal. Exact residues give the two-adic valuations.

The Version 9 construction retains the normalized generator, exponent-19 height, restricted converse, pole realization and Gaussian prime inputs. Direct targets remove division by four in local comparison; completeness uses the actual doubling images of reduction groups and compatible CRT congruences. The smaller anchor and changed scalar label require explicit local and height calculations rather than renamed indices.

The point-chart equivalence is specific to Q(sqrt2) and D=(3-sqrt2)^2. The square lemma uses Euclidean principality, unit signs, parity of every finite valuation and the exceptional residue field F7. Reversible ordinate cancellations require the proved nonzero h,j domains; no general square-abscissa characterization is assumed.

Shorter Laurent and preparation circuits retain inverse guards or derive their nonvanishing from existing equations. Each replacement has explicit forward and reverse rational witnesses and does not introduce zero branches.

The product-height identity is local at every place, using the formal open subgroup and compactness, nonsingular reduction at seven, and positivity of non-torsion doubles at both real embeddings. It concerns the field product, not its rational norm. This identity permits three positive-square scales while preserving the exponent-19 root-height constant and completeness order.

Odd-index enforcement uses the squareclass homomorphism with exceptional addition cases checked, the existing full Mordell–Weil description and independence of epsilon, minus one and d. Explicit halving formulas prove both projection directions. Only root points are augmented; shared and comparison indices need not be odd.
